articles.title: Dolly Parton Lands Three Posthumous Grammy Nominations
articles.summary: With the reveal of the 2027 Grammy nominations on Monday, Parton now has 58 total noms.
articles.content:
Dolly Parton has been posthumously nominated for three Grammy Awards .

The “Jolene” singer received two nods in the best country duo/group performance; the first stemming from her feature on Zac Brown's “Butterfly,” with the second hailing from her song “Light of a Clear Blue Morning” with Lainey Wilson, Miley Cyrus, Queen Latifah and Reba McEntire.

With the reveal of the 2027 Grammy nominations on Monday, Parton now has 58 total noms. She has previously won 10 Grammys , and received the Recording Academy's Lifetime Achievement Award in 2011. articles.title: Taylor Swift Scores Five Grammy Nominations, Including Album and Record of the Year Nods
articles.summary: Swift‘s 'The Life of a Showgirl' album and track for 'Toy Story 5' are among the nominations for the February 2027 show.
articles.content:
Taylor Swift is headed to the 2027 Grammy Awards as a five-time nominee.

Swift received five nominations including record of the year for "The Fate of Ophelia" and album of the year for The Life of a Showgirl . The Life of a Showgirl title track, which Swift performs with Sabrina Carpenter, is up for best pop duo/group performance. Meanwhile, her Toy Story 5 composition "I Knew It, I Knew You" was nominated in the song of the year and best song written for visual media categories.

During the livestream of the Grammy nominations, Swift made a surprise appearance to announce the last two categories, album and song of the year. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Music 2027 Grammy Nominations: Raye, Rosalía Lead a Women-Dominated General Field Music Grammy Nominations: Watch the Livestream

Last year, the singer-songwriter went home empty-handed despite receiving six nominations, including album of the year and best pop vocal album for The Tortured Poets Department .

Swift has already made Grammys history after winning the coveted the album of the year Grammy four times. Swift won album of the year for her albums Fearless in 2010 — she surpassed Alanis Morissette as the category's youngest victor at 20 years old — 1989 in 2015, folklore in 2021 and Midnights in 2024.

Swift and Adele are the only women to have taken home an award in this category more than once, with Adele winning for albums 21 and 25 . Meanwhile, Frank Sinatra, Stevie Wonder and Paul Simon have also won the album of the year award three times.

For Swift‘s The Life of a Showgirl , which was recorded in between show dates during the European leg of her record-breaking Eras tour, the superstar reteamed with producers Max Martin and Shellback, who worked with Swift on some of her biggest pop hits, including "Shake It Off," "Blank Space" and "I Knew You Were Trouble." She first revealed the project on Travis and Jason Kelce's New Heights podcast in August 2025. Just weeks after making the surprise announcement, Swift and Kelce revealed their engagement . The couple got married in July of this year. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Swift‘s "I Knew It, I Knew You" marked a return to Swift's country music roots with the singer-songwriter set to make her return to the CMA Awards stage after last performing there 13 years ago. The song, which has been considered a top contender for a song of the year Oscar nomination, is nominated for single of the year at the upcoming CMAs.

For the 2027 Grammys , female acts make up the leading nominees with Raye topping the nominations with 11 followed by Rosalía with nine; Ella Langley, Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo and Phoebe Bridgers with seven each; and Olivia Dean with six nods, tied with Bruno Mars and Leon Thomas.

This year's eligibility period includes recordings released from Aug. 31, 2025, through Aug. 28, 2026. Final round voting, in which Recording Academy voting members choose the Grammy winners, will take place between Dec. 10, 2026 and Jan. 7, 2027.

The 2027 Grammys will air on ABC, marking the first time in more than 50 years that the music awards show hasn't aired on its longtime home of CBS. The ceremony will premiere live across ABC, Disney+ and Hulu from Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Sunday, Feb. 7, 2027, at 7 p.m. ET / 4 p.m. PT.

articles.content:
The relationship between Fox News and President Donald Trump has been strained in recent months, but it clearly endures.

First Lady Melania Trump will take part in the Fox Corp.-backed outlet's seventh annual “All-American Christmas Tree Lighting,” slated to take place on Friday, November 20th at 5 p.m. eastern during a special edition of “ The Five .” Co-hosts Greg Gutfeld, Dana Perino, Harold Ford Jr., Jesse Watters and Emily Compagno will light the tree outside the network's New York City headquarters in an area that has been dubbed Fox Square Mrs. Trump will help children decorate a Christmas tree and share cookies and hot chocolate with them, while asking about their favorite holiday traditions and the things they like most about the season. Contemporary Christian singer Phil Wickman will contribute with live performances. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Glenn Close Says Her 'Career Is to Create Characters for Gay Halloween Parades' AFM Dealmakers, Talent Agents and Hollywood Stars Left Stranded by Nationwide Flight Stoppage

The Fox News All-American Christmas Tree will stand at 50 feet tall, and will be decorated with 18,000 ornaments and 340,000 warm white, true white and red lights. The tree is made by holiday lighting and display company American Christmas based in Mt. Vernon, N.Y., and will have a six-foot-tall dove topper with 4,800 embedded lights.

Mrs. Trump's appearance on Fox News comes after her husband, President Donald Trump, appeared to place some of the blame for Republicans being largely defeated by Democrats in the nation's recent midterm elections on the network itself. “FoxNews bears responsibility for these losses by constantly and consistently putting on the Dumocrat opposition, and worse,” Trump said via a post on Truth Social on the night of the elections. The Christmas special has become a regular part of the Fox News programming calendar, much like CNN's annual telecast of New Year's Eve festivities in Times Square is a bedrock element of its end-of-year schedule. CNN has recently tried to expand its hosting duo for that night, Anderson Cooper and Andy Cohen, to other holidays, such as the Fourth of July.

Guests in the past at the Fox News Christmas Tree Lighting have included Chris Tomlin and Gavin DeGraw.

Steve Doocy and Carley Shimkus will also participate in the evening. Doocy, a longtime co-host of “Fox & Friends,” will serve as “Christmas correspondent” for the evening, while Shimkus, a co-host of the early-morning “Fox & Friends First,” will lead social content. Both will offer viewers inside looks at Fox News Media studios along with exclusive interviews with special guests. Lauren Green, Fox News Channel 's chief religion correspondent, will introduce Reverend Franklin Graham and actor Jonathan Roumie as they offer a blessing to the audience.

Fox News Media has partnered with Armed Services YMCA, an organization dedicated to assisting junior enlisted service members and their families as they navigate deployments, relocations, and the everyday sacrifices of military life. FOX News Media employees helped pack stockings filled with gifts for deployed service members and wrote personalized welcome-home cards for troops returning for the holidays.

articles.title: Disney Reveals Hexed Will Be Their Last Movie With a Traditional Animation Style
articles.summary: Chief Creative Officer of Disney Animation Studios Jared Bush has just teased the end of a massive Disney animation era following the media giant's upcoming movie Hexed. Disney has pretty consistently received criticism of late, whether that's backlash to the company's many live-action remakes—the common refrain for which is they've done very little other than […]
articles.content:
For one thing, the cast is ridiculously star-studded, with the lead character, Billie, played by Hailee Steinfeld . Steinfeld is joined by major names like Rashida Jones, Alan Tudyk, Jodie Foster, Walter Goggins, and more. Additionally, and perhaps even more importantly, the movie's first trailer received surprisingly very positive comments from audiences, with some going as far as to say this could be the very change that Disney desperately needs right now. Unfortunately, Bush's latest comments suggesting that Hexed may be the last Disney movie with the traditional animation style could mean that the House of Mouse is heading into a real ‘out of the frying pan and into the fire' situation. Check out Bush's exact comments and what they might mean below.

Per Deadline , regarding Hexed and the future of Disney animation, Bush said, “ Frozen 3 is coming out next year. We have an all-new original called Clay the year after that, which is, like, our first major new art style. I should probably tell you, this year's movie, Hexed , which is an original, it may be our last original in the Disney art style as people know it. I think, beyond this, any original is going to be wildly different.” When pressed to explain what that meant, Bush added, “I think people will understand when they see a Disney original recently, like, oh, here's our CG animation style. That said, I think that the next several originals all have wildly different art styles. We're really going to be pushing into some new areas, so to me, it's a really exciting moment for us.”

Jared Bush shares updates on ‘Zootopia 3,’ ‘Frozen 3’ and ‘Hexed’ and reveals the new, upcoming animated films at Disney will have “wildly different art styles”: “We’re really going to be pushing into some new areas” | #GovernorsAwards pic.twitter.com/nw16Ci8WoD

As excited as Bush might be for this change, this update seems very likely to ruffle feathers. As much as Disney fans have complained about the live-action remakes not adding or changing enough to warrant a whole new movie, the fanbase is also known for being one driven by nostalgia—something that tends not to pair well with major changes or ends of eras such as the one Bush seems to suggest is coming. Granted, he only said that Hexed “may be” the last Disney animated movie in this art style given that the next several projects are “wildly different,” so there is a chance that this animation style will return, especially if the change is poorly received. For now, though, signs point towards a brand-new era for Disney.

articles.content:
Madonna is nominated for the 2027 Grammys in the dance/electronic categories for Confessions II , but her latest album didn't make it to the biggest categories.

The Grammy nods, the first for the pop superstar in 16 years, follow the release earlier this year of the 16-song Confessions II as a follow-up to the 2005 chart-topping original, Confessions on a Dance Floor . Madonna, who has seven Grammys under her belt, netted from Recording Academy voters nominations for best dance/electronic album for Confessions II , best dance/electronic recording for "I Feel So Free," and best dance pop recording for “Danceteria." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Music Ariana Grande Lands Four Grammy Nominations, Including Song of the Year Nod, After "Taking a Step Back From Visibility" Music Harry Styles Shut Out of the 2027 Grammy Nominations

Madonna also scored a Grammy nomination for best remixed recording for "Love Sensation," a collaboration on the Confessions II album with Kylie Minogue, and a best pop duo/group performance nomination along with Sabrina Carpenter for “Bring Your Love.” But despite buzz going into the Grammy nominations reveal on Monday morning, Confessions II was shut out of the all-important record of the year, song of the year and album of the year categories. The five nominations do, however, end a drought for Madonna as her last Grammy award came in 2010 with "Celebration" winning for best dance recording. Her 28 Grammy nominations and seven trophies over the course of her career have come mostly in the dance song and electronic album categories, where Madonna had her biggest haul on Monday.

articles.title: Grammys Snubs and Surprises: Harry Styles Shut Out, Raye's Huge Year and Noah Kahan Only Gets One Nomination
articles.summary: The 2027 Grammy nominations have arrived, with some notable breakthroughs and reigning hot streaks from artists including Raye, Rosalía, Phoebe Bridgers, Miranda Lambert, the Olivias (Dean and Rodrigo), Bruno Mars and many more. As with every year, there are plenty of surprises and just as many snubs among the nominees. Raye and Rosalía were among […]
articles.content:
The 2027 Grammy nominations have arrived , with some notable breakthroughs and reigning hot streaks from artists including Raye, Rosalía, Phoebe Bridgers, Miranda Lambert, the Olivias (Dean and Rodrigo), Bruno Mars and many more.

As with every year, there are plenty of surprises and just as many snubs among the nominees. Raye and Rosalía were among the artists who had the most unexpected success stories in the top categories, as were some best new artist nominees including Remi Wolf, Angine de Poitrine and the Womack Sisters. Women dominated across numerous categories, while artists like Ariana Grande and Stella Lefty had surprisingly lower-than-expected showings. Variety ticks down the nominees list to break down what was expected — and what wasn't. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 8 Standout Moments From the Governors Awards: Glenn Close Finally Gets Her Oscar, Diane Warren Pitches Olivia Wilde a Christmas Song and More 'Cher Adores Michael Douglas,' Icon's Rep Says After Douglas Disses Her Oscar Win for 'Moonstruck'

SNUB: Harry Styles shut out entirely. Perhaps the artist with one of the biggest years is also one of the biggest snubs among the 2027 Grammy nominees. Styles had been on a red-hot run amid the release of his fourth studio album “Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally.” He announced the record in January and followed with its lead single “Aperture,” leading into the March release of the project. He then spent the bulk of the year on the road as part of his “Together, Together” world tour that brought him to cities including Amsterdam, London, Mexico City, São Paulo and New York City, where he staged a historic 30-night residency at the famed Madison Square Garden through the end of October. However, the album itself met a polarized reaction, even from hardcore fans.

Among the categories where Styles submitted “KATTDO” were album of the year, best pop vocal album, best engineered album and best album cover. He submitted “Aperture” for record of the year, song of the year, best pop solo performance and best music video; “Coming Up Roses” for best arrangement, instruments, and vocals; and “One Night Only Manchester” for best music film. It's perplexing that the Recording Academy denied every submission, particularly considering that he has been a Grammy darling for years with nine nominations and three wins, including album of the year for “Harry's House” in 2023. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

SURPRISE: Best new artist category is an unpredictable mixed bag. No one should be surprised by many of these nominees — Ella Langley, Sienna Spiro, Don Toliver, Geese and Slayyyter were largely predicted to secure spots among the class of 2027 — yet it's the remaining artists that may have some heads scratching for casual music fans, although all certainly have passionate fan bases. Canadian sibling duo Angine de Poitrine has built a very dedicated following that is equally mesmerized by their hypnotic strain of math rock as they are by their black-and-white polka dot costumes. The Womack Sisters, meanwhile, made waves among retro R&B fans with their self-titled debut album that released in August (and yes, they come from a formidable legacy: daughters of singers Cecil and Linda Womack, and nieces of the legendary Bobby). And Remi Wolf, who has been an indie-pop darling since she started putting out music in 2019, is something of a curveball, considering that she released her latest album “Mud” outside of the Grammy submission window and, like many nominees in years past (and some others this year), is far from a new artist.

It's worth noting the slate of artists who were included in predictions lists from various publications and industry spectators that didn't make the cut. Malcolm Todd, who had a huge year with his June album “Do That Again,” was left off the ballot, as was his sister Audrey Hobert, whose excellent debut “Who's the Clown?” was released last year. Sam Fender, Role Model, Stella Lefty, Miles Caton and Bella Kay were also excluded from the category after making noise during the eligibility period.

SURPRISE: Raye leads with the most nominations …which is not entirely shocking, given the consistent goodwill towards Raye and critical praise for her sophomore album “This Music May Contain Hope,” which was released independently in March. The singer-songwriter, who was recently named Variety ‘s 2026 Hitmaker of the Year , leads overall nominations with a staggering 11 nods, trailed by Rosalía with nine and Ella Langley, Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo and Phoebe Bridgers with seven. Raye is nominated in all three eligible categories of the Big Four, including album of the year, plus song and record of the year for “Where Is My Husband!” (She was already nominated for best new artist in 2025.) She's also up for best pop solo performance for “Husband” and best pop duo/group performance for “Click Clack Symphony” featuring Hans Zimmer; best pop vocal album; best dance pop recording for “Life Boat”; best traditional pop vocal performance for “I Hate the Way I Look Today”; best music video for “Click Clack Symphony”; and best arrangement, instruments and vocals for “Click Clack Symphony.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The only category where she's nominated that may leave some Grammy scholars puzzled is her inclusion in songwriter of the year (non-classical), where she's up against Amy Allen, Edgar Barrera, Theron Thomas and Joybeth Taylor — which is confusing because the honor was intended to recognize songwriters whose work was largely recorded by others. Among her credits are five of her own songs, plus four others where she has a songwriting credit but is not the main artist (Amma's “God Be My Witness”; Halle and GloRilla's “Know About Me”; Sonny Fodera and Libianca's “Let Me Be in Your Arms”; and Say Now's “Supermarket”). According to Academy rules, songwriters must submit a minimum of four songs in which they're credited as a songwriter or co-writer, and songs where the songwriter was credited as a Primary or Featured Artist or Producer do not qualify to meet the minimum threshold. Translated to layman's terms, Raye qualifies in this category because she met the threshold with credits as a songwriter for other artists' songs.

SNUB: Noah Kahan receives only one nomination. It seemed as though the singer-songwriter may have been steeling himself — and prepping his fans — for Grammy disappointment on Sunday after he tweeted , “Whatever happens tomorrow I love you all and I have done everything I've ever needed to do in my career because of YOUR support. You guys are all I care about.” The reality may be even more sobering, considering that Kahan had a gargantuan year and was predicted to secure nominations in the top and genre categories. Instead, he only picks up a single nomination in best contemporary folk album for “The Great Divide: The Last of the Bugs,” the expanded edition of his fourth album that initially dropped in April. This really did seem to be his shot at Grammy glory, given he's only gotten two nods before (best new artist in 2024 and best country duo/group performance in 2025), but it looks like it's better luck next year for one Mr. Kahan.

SURPRISE-ISH: Major female dominance in top categories. Really not much of a surprise, considering the large swath of female artists who gave the industry a run for its money over the past year. Six out of eight record of the year nominees are songs by women (the seventh, Tame Impala's “Dracula,” features Jennie). Bruno Mars is the only man to be nominated for album of the year with “The Romantic,” up against Phoebe Bridgers, Raye, Olivia Rodrigo, Olivia Dean, Rosalía, Ella Langley and Taylor Swift. Seven out of eight of the song of the year nominees are by women (Mars, again, offers a speck of diversity). And girl power isn't just limited to the biggest categories: all of the nominees in best dance pop recording, best R&B solo performance, best traditional pop vocal performance and best contemporary country album are by women. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

SNUB: Ariana Grande picks up fewer than expected. Admittedly, Grande hasn't historically been a heavily nominated artist. The most nods she received in one year was in 2020, when she picked up five. But given how well her latest album “Petal” performed, as did its lead single “Hate That I Made You Love Me,” Grande was expected to have a stronger showing for the 2027 awards. Next year, she'll be competing in four categories: song of the year for “Hate That I Made You Love Me,” best pop vocal album for “Petal,” best traditional pop vocal performance for “For Good” with Cynthia Erivo and best music video for “Hate That I Made You Love Me.” (“Petal” is up for a fifth award, in best immersive audio album, though Grande herself is not nominated.) This is certainly a snub for Grande who, despite picking up some substantial nods, was left out of album of the year, record of the year and all the other genre categories she submitted — surprising, considering that artists like Taylor Swift, Olivia Rodrigo and Rosalía got nominated in all three major categories where they were eligible.

SURPRISE: Speaking of, Rosalía's “Berghain,” hardly a traditional mainstream single, gets nods for record and song of the year. You'd be hard-pressed to find anyone who doesn't consider Rosalía's “Lux” to be a pop masterpiece, yet many of those same folks would probably agree that “Berghain” is far from what you'd consider a “mainstream” single. The track, featuring Björk and Yves Tumor, is like a 21st-century cantata, replete with vamping strings and ominous choral chants. Even with a cursory glance at the song and record of the year nominees, “Berghain” sticks out like a sore thumb, showing that genuine musicians are voting and appreciate the artistry of Rosalía's production and songwriting.

SNUB: Stella Lefty's “Boston,” one of the biggest singles of the year, gets ignored. Following in Alex Warren's “Ordinary” footsteps from earlier this year, Stella Lefty's “Boston” may be one of the biggest songs of 2026, but that is of little concern to voting members. The track has been a commercial juggernaut, reaching No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100, yet has been consistently dogged by accusations of plagiarism, as fans have noted its striking similarities to Kahan's “Stick Season.” Academy members fell in line with the critical consensus, it seems… And while Warren may have ended up with at least one nomination for best new artist, Lefty comes up empty-handed for next year.

articles.title: Patrick Stewart's Secret Comedy Roles Deserve To Be Part of His Legacy Alongside Star Trek & X-Men
articles.summary: Patrick Stewart’s legacy is largely tied to his role as Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek and Professor Charles Xavier in X-Men, with his last acting appearance premiering in December with Avengers: Doomsday. His voice is distinct, standing out among his peers, and casual viewers no doubt associate the actor with seriousness. However, for Stewart’s whole […]
articles.content:
However, for Stewart’s whole career, he had wanted to do comedy. He was rarely cast in comedy roles. During his career with the Royal Shakespeare Company, he was cast as Touchstone, the fool of Duke Frederick, for the 1968 production of As You Like It. Touchstone is typically a comedy role, given that he’s a jester. The director for As You Like It had a different take on the character, however, envisioning him as a sad, old man. It was that version of the character that the director felt Stewart would be perfect for.

Still, through collaborations with Seth MacFarlane , known for the television shows Family Guy and American Dad , and Ricky Gervais, audiences saw another side of Patrick Stewart — a comedic one. Stewart’s wit could be used for humor, and although the roles were never quite as popular as Picard and Xavier, they deserve to be part of Patrick Stewart’s legacy.

Patrick Stewart often credited Seth MacFarlane with having the greatest impact on his career regarding comedy. MacFarlane helped people see that there was another actor inside Patrick Stewart. Since his days at the Royal Shakespeare Company, other actors loved saying lines in Stewart’s voice, finding amusement, but they didn’t find Stewart himself funny.

Stewart had recurring voice roles in MacFarlane projects such as Family Guy and American Dad. For American Dad , Stewart voiced the inner thoughts of Baby Susie Swanson. Baby Susie was too young to speak, with her dialogue on the show mainly being noises voiced by Christina Milian. However, the show sometimes highlighted her inner thoughts. Not only were they in Patrick Stewart’s voice, but Stewart broke the fourth wall, directly asking the audience, “How are you liking the program so far?” In American Dad , Stewart wasn’t working against his voice, but rather it was working for him. It’s funny to think about a little girl’s thoughts coming out in the voice of Patrick Stewart, and to think that even a shred of Stewart’s consciousness doesn’t mind being trapped in said brain.

Additionally, Stewart acted in the sitcom Blunt Talk , which aired for two seasons between 2015 and 2016 and was executive produced by McFarlane. Blunt Talk featured Stewart as Walter Blunt — who shared the name of Stewart’s first role with the Royal Shakespeare Company, Sir Walter Blunt of Henry IV, Part I — who was a British newscaster who moved to LA. Blunt’s main ambition through the series was to conquer American nightly news, but he quickly found out that his goal was harder to achieve than initially thought.

Blunt Talk was met with mixed reviews from critics, with many believing the show mistook being vulgar for being witty in its comedy. Still, it was undeniable that Blunt Talk positioned Stewart as he hadn’t been before. Blunt Talk’s home network of Starz allowed the show to go to extreme places audiences hadn’t quite associated Stewart with, whether it was struggling in an airport men’s stall or in vulgar sexual encounters. Even if the show might not have been good, it’s worth checking out for Stewart’s performance.

In 2005, Patrick Stewart guest-starred in an episode of Ricky Gervais’s Extras. Stewart had been a fan of Gervais’s since The Office , finding the show genius, and couldn’t believe what he was hearing when Gervais called. Apparently, Stewart had a friend who loved doing impressions of famous people on the phone, so Stewart had assumed it wasn’t Gervais calling.

For Extras , Stewart played an exaggerated version of himself alongside Gervais’s role of a young actor still starting out who was cast as an extra in a production. Stewart gives him advice, emphasizing the impact of writing your own screenplay, and is very candid when Gervais asks about it. Taking inspiration from his character Charles Xavier in X-Men , Stewart’s exaggerated self wrote a screenplay about what it’d be like to have telepathy and telekinesis in the real world, one without superheroes. Stewart reveals that his character in the script is obsessed with undressing women. The episode plays the character’s stonefaced seriousness around being a perv for comedy, with even Gervais assuming Stewart must be joking.

In Patrick Stewart: A Knight of Comedy , Stewart delivered his own eulogy, which quickly devolved into a tale of previous sexual exploits. What starts with Stewart talking big about himself — calling himself “the greatest actor ever” — turns into stories throughout his life of having sex with inanimate objects, including the variety of props at the RSC.

Which Patrick Stewart comedy role made you laugh the hardest? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: Franco-Moroccan Director Nabil Ayouch on Exploring ‘More Intimacy in My Characters’ With Next Film ‘Run, With No Tears’
articles.summary: For Franco-Moroccan filmmaker Nabil Ayouch, the freedom to tell the stories in which he believes has always mattered more than winning universal approval. Over nearly three decades, he has built a career exploring complex social realities and giving a voice to characters determined to challenge the limits imposed upon their lives. Along the way, he […]
articles.content:
For Franco-Moroccan filmmaker Nabil Ayouch , the freedom to tell the stories in which he believes has always mattered more than winning universal approval. Over nearly three decades, he has built a career exploring complex social realities and giving a voice to characters determined to challenge the limits imposed upon their lives. Along the way, he has learned to embrace the possibility that his films won't always be understood.

"Making films means taking the risk of being misunderstood," Ayouch tells Variety at the 47th Cairo Intl. Film Festival, where he serves as president of the international competition jury and was honored with the Golden Pyramid Lifetime Achievement Award at the festival's opening ceremony. "Everyone wants to be loved. But if all I wanted was to be loved, I think I'd do something other than cinema." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Cher Adores Michael Douglas,' Icon's Rep Says After Douglas Disses Her Oscar Win for 'Moonstruck' Hollywood Still Faces Weekend Disruptions After FAA Lifts Flight Ground Stop

"It's more important for me to express myself, to say what I have to say, to try to be understood, to touch souls, than to be loved," he adds.

His return to Cairo carries particular significance. Nearly three decades ago, Ayouch presented his debut feature, "Mektoub," at the festival, where it won two awards. Since then, he has returned several times, drawn to a city whose energy he describes as both overwhelming and exhilarating.

But the convictions that first drove Ayouch to make films remain as strong as ever. "The rage that has driven me since I started making cinema is intact, perhaps even stronger today," he reflects, pointing to the injustices he sees around the world. "Every morning, I wake up full of this energy, this anger, but also full of love and passion for human beings. I want to continue seeing the beauty of this world and telling it through films." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

That tension between anger and hope has its roots in Ayouch's childhood in Sarcelles, a working-class suburb north of Paris, where he spent his formative years. He credits the teachers and youth workers at a local youth and cultural center with helping him channel difficult experiences into something constructive.

"They taught me how to transform things that hurt me and that rage into a saving energy," he recalls. "I don't think I would have become a director" without them.

The experience has shaped not only his filmmaking but also his efforts to support emerging talent. Ayouch has opened seven cultural centers across Morocco, hoping to offer young people opportunities similar to those that changed his own life.

His films, from "Ali Zaoua" and "Casablanca Beats" to "Much Loved" and "Everybody Loves Touda," have consistently focused on people seeking to take control of their own lives. But Ayouch resists defining his characters solely through their suffering.

"I need to meet someone whose soul attracts me, not simply because they've had a difficult life, but because of their desire to escape a cage, to break free from something that confines them," he says. "I don't like characters who are victims."

Ayouch believes his refusal to portray women as powerless was a key reason "Much Loved," his 2015 drama about sex workers in Marrakech, sparked such controversy in Morocco.

"Things would have been much simpler if the women in the film had been poor women who were beaten from beginning to end," he says. "It's because they're seeking independence, because they're demanding and want to escape their circumstances, that the film caused so much trouble."

The controversy surrounding "Much Loved" prompted moments of doubt, but Ayouch insists that provoking outrage has never been his objective.

"I don't make films to create controversy," he maintains. "I make films because something outrages me, and I can't imagine that those films won't be divisive."

Ayouch is a member of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences and France's Académie des Césars. As president of Cairo's international competition jury, he prefers to enter screenings knowing as little as possible about the filmmakers or their stories. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"I like to be surprised," he says. "Cinema is an encounter, a shock, a moment of wonder." He is particularly drawn to films that continue to reveal themselves long after the credits roll.

When it comes to jury deliberations, he favors discussion and consensus over voting, hoping that the jury's diverse perspectives will help them reach a collective decision rather than one imposed by majority rule.

Despite receiving a lifetime achievement award, Ayouch is hardly ready to call it a day. He jokingly dubbed it a "mid-lifetime achievement award," making clear that he hopes to have plenty more films ahead of him.

Looking ahead, he is interested in a different approach. "I'd like to explore a little more intimacy in my characters," he reveals. "To make cinema that's less political, and to find politics elsewhere, particularly in intimacy."

That exploration will continue with his next feature, "Run, With No Tears," which is scheduled to begin shooting in Morocco in early January. The film will star Vimala Pons, who replaces the previously announced Noomi Rapace, alongside Maryam Touzani and Nisrin Erradi, reuniting Ayouch with two actresses from his previous work. The film will be produced via his company Ali n' Productions.

While he is eager to explore new directions, Ayouch has little interest in revisiting or correcting his earlier work. "If I had to remake the films I've made, I'd remake them all, scene by scene, film by film, and change absolutely nothing."

articles.title: Anthony Mackie Defends His Viral Comments About Vision And Doomsday (But Do We Believe Him?)
articles.summary: So is Paul Bettany actually in Doomsday?
articles.content:
It's an exciting time to be a Marvel fans, given the release of VisionQuest' s finale for those with a Disney+ subscription , as well as the upcoming Marvel movie Avengers: Doomsday being a month and change away from its release. Just last week, Anthony Mackie went viral for seemingly spoiling Paul Bettany's role in Doomsday , but now he's defending those comments. The question is: do we actually believe him?

This potentially offers some much-needed context about Mackie's viral comments about hanging out with Paul Bettany while shooting Doomsday . If the actor is to be believed, he knew that VisionQuest was also shooting at Pinewood Studios in the U.K. at the same time as principal photography for the next Avengers flick. That's how he was able to see his frequent co-star, instead of shooting the crossover event together.

The "I guess" certainly doesn't inspire confidence. Given Marvel's tight security , actors sometimes have to tell white lies in order to guard the shared universe's spoilers. Case in point: Andrew Garifeld lied about returning as Spider-Man for years ahead of No Way Home 's release. As such, we're going to have to wait until the next Avengers movie hits theaters to find out whether or not Mackie was telling the truth about Bettany (and Holland).

articles.title: Golshifteh Farahani and Director Chabname Zariab on Anti-Taliban Film ‘When She Hears the Bells,’ Sold by Le Pacte
articles.summary: TALLINN, Estonia — The striking images of Kabul international airport stormed by thousands of Afghans and foreigners desperately trying to be evacuated by U.S. planes as Kabul fell into the hands of the Taliban, have stayed etched in many people’s minds. For Afghan-born Paris-based writer and director Chabname Zariad, long-listed for an Oscar with her […]
articles.content:
TALLINN, Estonia — The striking images of Kabul international airport stormed by thousands of Afghans and foreigners desperately trying to be evacuated by U.S. planes as Kabul fell into the hands of the Taliban, have stayed etched in many people's minds.

For Afghan-born Paris-based writer and director Chabname Zariad, long-listed for an Oscar with her short film "Hizia," the takeover of Afghanistan from the hard-line Islamist group, was a gut-wrenching experience that immediately triggered her desire to spotlight in a movie their authoritarian regime and especially crackdown on women. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Taylor Swift and Karlie Kloss Reunite at Travis Kelce’s Chiefs Game Against Jets Taylor Swift to Perform at CMAs for the First Time in 13 Years

That film -"When She Hears the Bells" ("Les clochettes de Kaboul”) is now an intense thriller drama shepherded by France's Alta Rocca Films and repped by Le Pacte , with star-actress Goldshifteh Farahani ("Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales," "Alpha") in the title role. Co-producing partners take in Belgium's Versus Production, Germany's Starhaus Filmproduktion and Arte France Cinéma. Both Zariab and Farahani are in Tallinn for the film's world premiere on Nov. 18 at the Black Nights Film Festival's first feature competition .

The film, penned by the filmmaker with her sister Parande Zariab, is set in the Summer of 2021, as Kabul is on the verge of falling into the hands of the Taliban. We follow the young widow Leila (Farahani), who arrives in Kabul and starts working in a kitchen, set in a "Bacha Bazi" house.

The term (literally meaning playing with boys in Persian) refers to a controversial yet still practiced tradition in Central Asia, "particularly in conservative and religious countries," notes Zariab, whereby young boys, dressed as women, are forced to dance in front of men, and are subject to all kind of abuses. In the film, Leila decides to help a group of Bacha Bazi boys flee their horrendous fate, as Kabul edges closer to collapse. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Speaking with Variety on the near eve of the film's world premiere, the director says she returned to the topic of the Bacha Bazi – depicted in her 2015 short film "When You Hear the Bells" – not to further dig into the subject but to use it as a symbol of the state of a complex society under Taliban rule. "In reality, when you remove women from the public sphere, you also repress the desire for them which leaves room for all types of abuses. It becomes a sick society," she notes.

To raise awareness on the topic and attract the largest audience possible, Zariab and her sister borrowed from genre codes. The helmer who referenced Tarik Saleh's films and Saeed Roustayi's Cannes-selected "Leila's Brothers," said once she had built the form, the substance fell into place.

Hiring French-based Iranian actress Farahani for the title role was "an obvious choice."

"Ever since I had seen Golshifteh in Asghar Farhadi's "About Elly, " I had followed her career and in Atiq Rahimi's "The Patience Stone," she spoke an impeccable authentic Afghan Persian. Then her activism for women's rights also played a major part for me. Not only did she deliver an exceptional performance, but her professionalism on set was astonishing," says the helmer who cast her against mostly Afghan theatre actors and non-professionals to keep it authentic.

Farahani on Her Motivation Sharing with Variety why she boarded the project, Farahani says: "First of course, it was the powerful, well-written script and the humanitarian message behind it. The story needed to be told. Second, it was the incredible perseverance of Chabname who never gave up on me. And finally, it was that inner feeling telling me there was no way I could skip this one. As if it were simply part of what was written."

About her character Leila, the actress, who was bestowed Locarno Festival's prestigious Excellence Award, Davide Campari in 2025 , says she was compelled by "her ability to adapt and change. It reflects something you see so much in this region: how most people specially women can evolve in ways you might never imagine when they are forced to survive.

“It also reveals the potential within every human being to be pushed to the edge and find absolute courage, driven by dignity and human values. From a frightened, lonely woman to a lioness who decides to change the destiny of these [Bacha Bazi] children, even at the risk of her own life." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Farahani says working with children and first-time actors was both a challenge and a blessing in disguise. "When it works at its best, it becomes one of the most pleasant and rewarding parts of the job. They can become the most wonderful acting partners," she says, citing in particular the impeccable performance from Fatima Tawakkuli who plays Leila's co-worker and friend Mari, and newcomer Mojtaba Ahmadi, aka the elder Basha Bazi dancer Tamin.

Zariab says the initial plan was to shoot in Iraqi Kurdistan which bears resemblance to Afghanistan, but when bombing between Israel and Iran started in 2024, the movie eventually rolled in Morocco. To capture wide shots of Kabul, she asked a friend cinematographer in Afghanistan to fill in.

For her feature debut, the helmer is grateful for the support she got from her entire team, especially Farahani, cinematographer Pierre Cottereau ("Café de Flore"), and her first AD Benjamin Blanc.

On the production front, she cites French producers Lou Chicoteaux and Jean-Etienne Brat of Alta Rocca Films (behind her 2020 short “Hizia"), Arte Cinéma and Le Pacte –~in charge of sales and French distribution – as "truly exceptional partners who understood the urgency of this film and the significance of its subject matter." "I'm well aware that I was fortunate to have such a substantial budget [€3.5 million or $3.8 million) for my debut, especially at a time when funding is tightening across the board," concedes Zariab.

Chicoteaux and Brat also admit that "getting people on board this wild adventure" was not an easy ride. "Yet we had a director whose legitimacy was beyond question as she herself had fled her home country because of the Taliban. From the West, she watched her nation suffer and sink into despair and had to make this film," Brat explains.

Ultimately for him, "beyond the Bacha Bazi phenomenon which serves as potent symbol for the deviations that can emerge in societies undergoing intense radicalisation," "When She Hears the Bells "is at its core "the story of a woman who risks her own life to save children; She emerges as a true heroine." Commenting on the pic's resistance statement, Farahani adds: "Artists tell stories about these horrors and make people pay attention to what is happening in our world. I feel their work is more important than what politicians do. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Artists create bridges, while politicians and extremists create separation and duality. Artists try to make people identify with one another, despite geographical and cultural differences, through universal human values: love, loyalty, integrity, etc.," she says.

"People may be poor in regions and countries like Afghanistan, but that doesn't mean they lack dignity or wisdom. Art helps polish people's judgements, often shaped by propaganda, into something more human, nuanced and real," she concludes. Following its run in Tallinn, "When She Hears the Bell" will compete at the Torino Film Festival.

articles.title: Ariana Grande Lands Four Grammy Nominations, Including Song of the Year Nod, After "Taking a Step Back From Visibility"
articles.summary: The nominations come months after the 'Wicked' star released her eighth studio album, 'Petal,' and wrapped up her Eternal Sunshine Tour.
articles.content:
Ariana Grande has received four nominations for the 2027 Grammys .

Grande's nominations, which were announced Monday morning, include a song of the year nod for “Hate That I Made You Love Me,” which also scored a best music video nod, as well as noms for best pop vocal album ( Petal ) and best traditional pop vocal performance for her “For Good” duet from Wicked: For Good alongside Cynthia Erivo.

In the song of the year category, Grande is nominated alongside Rosalía's “Berghain,” Ella Langley's “Choosin' Texas,” Olivia Rodrigo's “The Cure,” Taylor Swift's “I Knew It, I Knew You,” Olivia Dean's “Man I Need,” Bruno Mars' “Risk It All” and Raye's “Where Is My Husband!” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Music 2027 Grammy Nominations: Raye, Rosalía Lead a Women-Dominated General Field Music Grammy Nominations: Watch the Livestream

Most of Grande's nominations come in support of her eighth studio album, Petal , released July 31. The 12-track album debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200.

The singer has previously won three Grammys . She earned her first in 2019 for best pop vocal album for Sweetener , followed by best pop duo/group performance for “Rain on Me” with Lady Gaga in 2021 and, earlier this year, for her and Erivo's “Defying Gravity” from the first Wicked film.

The 2027 Grammy nominations come more than two months after Grande wrapped up her Eternal Sunshine Tour , with her final performance taking place in London on Sept. 1. Her 2024 album, Eternal Sunshine, earned three Grammy nominations but was shut out at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards .

In recent years, Grande has also returned to acting, starring as Glinda the Good Witch in Jon M. Chu's Wicked (2024) and Wicked: For Good (2025). The role earned her an Oscar nomination for best supporting actress at the 97th Academy Awards. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

articles.content:
Kino Lorber has picked up U.S. distribution rights to Edward Said: Between Worlds , Maiken Baird's archival documentary on the influential Palestinian scholar and activist. Kino Lorber is planning a 2027 theatrical release for the film.

Baird, an executive producer of projects like Bryan Fogel's Oscar-winning Icarus (2017) and Orwell: 2+2=5 (2025) from Raoul Paul, drew on extensive archive footage, including home movies, rare television appearances and public debates, to trace the evolution of Said's thought and his political awakening. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV 'Slow Horses' Lands Early Renewal for Seasons 9 and 10 at Apple TV Movies Gerard Depardieu Drops Appeal Against Sexual Assault Conviction, Admits Guilt

The documentary, made in collaboration with the Said family and his estate , spans seven decades from Said's childhood in Jerusalem to his migration, first to Egypt during the 1948 Palestine war, and finally to the United States, where Said became a noted academic in comparative literature at Columbia University. A prominent academic and cultural critic, Said was among the founders of the field of post-colonial studies. His 1978 book Orientalism, which critiqued Western cultural representations of the Eastern world, was a foundational text. The film also tracks Said's work as an activist, including his long-time advocacy for a Palestinian state, and his extensive efforts in the media to explain Palestinian history to a Western public.

“Shortly after October 7th, I found myself missing Edward Said – his voice, humanity and his remarkable powers of speech on Palestinian history and struggle for self-determination,” Baird sasid in a statement. “This film is both a reminder of Edward Said's brilliance and an introduction for a new generation who care deeply about the necessity of Palestinian rights.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

articles.content:
What is perhaps most remarkable about the overwhelmingly female-dominated list of 2027 Grammy nominations is the fact that perennials Taylor Swift , Beyonce and Adele actually aren't leading the pack.

While Beyonce and Adele were basically off-cycle in 2026 (Beyonce did get a nod for a previously unreleased bonus track for her "Bday" anniversary reissue), make no mistake, it's another huge year for Swift — her five nominations bring her overall total to 63, with 14 wins, and she's the only artist in history to win album of the year four times: in 2010 for "Fearless," 2016 for "1989," 2021 for "Folklore" and 2024 for "Midnights," surpassing three-peaters Frank Sinatra, Stevie Wonder and Paul Simon. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Taylor Swift to Perform at CMAs for the First Time in 13 Years 'Hunger Games' Companion Album to Feature Jennifer Lawrence, Ella Langley, Tyler Childers, Mckenna Grace and 25 More

Her nod this year in that same category for her latest full-length, "The Life of a Showgirl," makes her only the second artist in history to receive that nomination for five consecutive studio albums, joining Kendrick Lamar — although he actually has never won that prize.

And although Swift's total 2027 tally was topped by Raye (11), Rosalia (9), Phoebe Bridgers, Miranda Lambert, Ella Langley, Olivia Rodrigo (7 each), Olivia Dean and, oh yeah, two dudes, Bruno Mars and Leon Thomas (6 each), she's not lacking in big looks: She scored a total of five major nods, three of them in the "big four" categories: along with album, she's up for record of the year ("The Fate of Ophelia") and song of the year ("I Knew It, I Knew You," from "Toy Story 5"), as well as pop duo (for the album's title track, a duet with Sabrina Carpenter) and song for visual media (also “I Knew It, I Knew You”). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

At this point, Swift is such a dominant artist that her past victories actually may be working against her — after a record four album of the year wins, voters may think, "Let's give someone else a shot this year" — but it seems very unlikely that she will walk away from the 2027 Grammys empty-handed.

articles.title: 2027 Grammy Nominations: Raye, Rosalía Lead a Women-Dominated General Field
articles.summary: Raye earned 11 nominations and Rosalía got nine, while Olivia Rodrigo, Ella Langley and Phoebe Bridgers tied with seven each. Olivia Dean earned six.
articles.content:
Raye is the top nominee heading into the 2027 Grammy Awards — with Rosalía, Ella Langley , Olivia Rodrigo , Phoebe Bridgers and Olivia Dean not far behind — as women dominate the noms in the major categories for this year's awards, revealed during the Grammys ‘ livestream Monday morning.

Raye earned 11 nominations, including for record and song of the year with “Where is my Husband!,” and for album of the year for This Music May Contain Hope . Rosalía got nine nominations with her heavily lauded Lux, which also got an album of the year nod, while single “Berghain” is up for record and song of the year. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Music Grammy Nominations: Watch the Livestream Movies Governors Awards: Glenn Close, Ridley Scott and Floyd Norman Accept Honorary Oscars, Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler Receive Thalberg Award

The Grammys themselves will take place Feb. 7 at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, with this year's ceremony airing live at 7 p.m. ET / 4 p.m. PT on the Disney-owned ABC and streaming on Disney+ and Hulu. The 2027 Grammys will be the first in more than 50 years not to air on the music awards show's longtime home of CBS.

"It's a privilege to congratulate all the incredible music creators recognized in this year's Grammy nominations," Harvey Mason Jr., Grammys CEO, said in a statement. "From first-time nominees to artists reaching career milestones, it's inspiring to see musicians at every stage of their careers represented. Together, they reflect the extraordinary diversity of genres, crafts and backgrounds that make up our community. We look forward to a remarkable season of celebration, and I'm grateful to our voting members for their continued commitment to honoring the music that moves us year after year."

Langley, Rodrigo , Bridgers and Miranda Lambert all tied for the third-most nominations this year with seven each. Langley's “Choosin' Texas” got record and song of the year nods, while her second album Dandelion is up for album of the year, and she's also up for best new artist. (Lambert earned four of her nominations, including producer of the year, for her work with Langley on Dandelion and “Choosin' Texas.”) Rodrigo's You Seem Pretty Sad For a Girl So in Love is up for album of the year, while “The Cure” is up for record and song of the year. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Bridgers' Lost Weekend earned an album of the year nomination, her second time nominated in the category after Boygenius' The Record was nominated in 2024. Olivia Dean, last year's best new artist winner, earned six nominations, with The Art of Loving up for album of the year while “Man I Need” is up for record and song of the year. Taylor Swift got five nominations, as The Life of a Showgirl is up for album of the year, while “The Fate of Ophelia” was nominated for record of the year and her Toy Story 5 track “I Knew It, I Knew You” is up for song of the year.

Bruno Mars is the lone male artist in this year's album of the year race with The Romantic , his first solo album since 2016. The album's lead single “I Just Might” nabbed a record of the year nomination, while “Risk It All” is up for song of the year.

In the the record of the year race, 2027 Coachella headliner Tame Impala rounds out the category with “Dracula,” his hit with K-Pop superstar Jennie. Meanwhile in the song of the year race, Ariana Grande took the last spot with “Hate That I Made You Love Me,” her first-ever nomination in the category and her first nomination in the general field for her solo work since Thank U, Next was nominated for album of the year back in 2020.

In the best new artist category, Langley, whose “Choosin' Texas” broke the record for most-ever weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, is joined by Sienna Spiro, Angine de Poitrine, Geese, Slayyyter, Don Toliver, Remi Wolf and the Womack Sisters. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

For producer of the year, Lambert is up against Tony Berg, Noah Goldstein, Mike Sabath and Dernst “D'Mile” Emile. She's joined by Edgar Barrera, Joybeth Taylor, 2024 winner Theron Thomas and Amy Allen, who's looking to win in the category for a third consecutive year.

Outside of the major categories, Leon Thomas, one of the top nominees of last year's Grammy season, nabbed six more noms this year, all across the R&B categories. The pop and rock/alternative categories look particularly competitive, with Grande, Raye, Rodrigo, Dean and Mars all up for pop vocal album.

For best rock album, The Rolling Stones' Foreign Tongues , is up against Jack White's Frozen Charlotte, Angine de Poitrine's Vol.II, Foo Fighters' Your Favorite Toy and Muse's The Wow! Signal . For alternative, Bridgers' Lost Weekend and Rosalía's Lux are joined by Geese's Getting Killed, Gorillaz's Mountain , Alabama Shakes' I Must Be Dreaming and Charli XCX's Music. Fashion. Film. (Charli has two albums up for Grammys this year, as her Wuthering Heights soundtrack album is up for best compilation soundtrack for visual media.)

Rap was underrepresented in the general field this year compared to last, when three rap albums made it to the album of the year race. Toliver is the lone hip-hop act in the general field this time.

As for what's not included, BTS is the most notable holdout of the season, deciding not to submit amid the newly-introduced Asian pop music performance category, with the group's members saying in statements that they hope “music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

articles.title: Bryan Cranston & Marianne Jean-Baptiste Heading To Broadway In Ivo Van Hove's Acclaimed 'All My Sons' Revival
articles.summary: Director Ivo Van Hove's acclaimed, Olivier Award-winning West End revival of Arthur Miller's All My Sons starring Bryan Cranston and Marianne Jean-Baptiste will transfer to Broadway this spring, producers announced today. The production, with Cranston and Jean-Baptiste reprising their roles of the play's Joe and Kate Keller characters, will begin performances at Broadway’s August Wilson […]
articles.content:
Director Ivo Van Hove ‘s acclaimed, Olivier Award-winning West End revival of Arthur Miller's All My Sons starring Bryan Cranston and Marianne Jean-Baptiste will transfer to Broadway this spring, producers announced today.

The production, with Cranston and Jean-Baptiste reprising their roles of the play's Joe and Kate Keller characters, will begin performances at Broadway's August Wilson Theatre on Tuesday, March 30, 2027, with an opening night set for Tuesday, April 13, 2027.

Additional casting will be announced at a later date. Related Stories News 'Downstate' Broadway Review: Provocative Play About Sex Offenders Questions The Nature Of Forgiveness News Steve Carell & John C. Reilly To Star In 'The Odd Couple' Broadway Revival This Spring

"We are thrilled to bring this Olivier Award-winning production to Broadway following its acclaimed run in London, where audiences connected with Arthur Miller's masterpiece in powerful and deeply resonant ways," said producers Wessex Grove and Gavin Kalin Productions. "Led by the extraordinary Bryan Cranston and Marianne Jean-Baptiste and brought to life by Ivo Van Hove and an exceptional design team, this production offers a compelling examination of the American Dream and the cost of putting self-interest above collective responsibility.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

The producers' statement continued, “At a moment when Miller's questions of accountability, truth, and moral responsibility feel more urgent than ever, we look forward to sharing this timely and deeply moving production with New York audiences."

The production will feature scenic and lighting design by Jan Versweyveld and costume design by An D'Huys, both longtime collaborator of Van Hove. Sound design will be by Tom Gibbons, last on Broadway with Every Brilliant Thing and attached to the upcoming Small Mouth Sounds .

Including its original 1947 production, All My Sons has been staged on Broadway four times, most recently in Jack O'Brien's 2019 staging starring Tracy Letts and Annette Bening.

The official synopsis: “Respected, self-made businessman Joe prides himself on providing for his wife and their two sons. While wartime delivers profits for the family, it comes at a price when his partner is charged with criminal manufacturing deals, and his eldest son goes missing in action. Peacetime brings little peace of mind as Joe's true involvement in the activity begins to surface, and he is suddenly confronted by the consequences of his actions. Arthur Miller skewers the dishonest promise of the American Dream in this disturbingly prescient play.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Breaking Bad star Cranston was last on Broadway in Van Hove's Network (2018), in which he played the disturbed and doomed TV news anchor Howard Beale. He played President Lyndon Baines Johnson in 2014's All The Way, and was a producer on the 2015 musical Finding Neverland.

Jean-Baptiste, Oscar-nominated for 1997's Secrets & Lies and a series regular on CBS' Without A Trace , will be making her Broadway debut with All My Sons (though she has appeared in two 2010 Off Broadway productions for The Public Theater's Shakespeare in the Park – The Winter's Tale and The Merchant of Venice) . Her UK stage credits go back to 1990 up to her performance in All My Sons .

The West End All My Sons production won the Olivier for Best Revival, as did supporting actor Paapa Essiedu, with Van Hove, Cranston and Jean-Baptiste receiving nominations.

The revival is produced by Wessex Grove (Benjamin Lowy, Emily Vaughan-Barratt, Tom Powis) and Gavin Kalin Productions.

articles.title: Bryan Cranston, Marianne Jean-Baptiste to Star in 'All My Sons' on Broadway
articles.summary: The two reprise their roles from the Olivier Award-winning London production.
articles.content:
Bryan Cranston and Marianne Jean-Baptiste will star in All My Sons on Broadway this spring.

The two reprise their roles as Joe Keller and Kate Keller after the play's Olivier Award-winning run in London last season. Ivo van Hove directs the Arthur Miller revival, which is set to begin performances March 30, 2027 at Broadway's August Wilson Theatre, ahead of an April 13 opening night.

Additional casting will be announced at a later date. Paapa Essiedu also starred in the London cast and won an Olivier Award for his performance, in addition to the play's win for best revival.

Cranston returns to Broadway after last starring in van Hove's Network in 2018 and winning a Tony Award for his role. He made his debut as President Lyndon B. Johnson in All The Way, for which he also won a Tony Award.

This is the Broadway debut for Jean-Baptiste, who received an Academy Award nomination for her performance in Mike Leigh's Secrets & Lies, and recently appeared in his 2025 feature Hard Truths .

Van Hove, known for his spare, innovative style that typically involves the use of cameras, was last on Broadway with his updated take on West Side Story, which saw its run cut short by the pandemic.

All My Sons follows businessman Joe Keller as he grapples with the fallout of World War II, including the loss of a son and his own actions during the war. Originally premiering in 1947, the play was last on Broadway in 2019, starring Tracy Letts and Annette Bening.

"We are thrilled to bring this Olivier Award-winning production to Broadway following its acclaimed run in London, where audiences connected with Arthur Miller's masterpiece in powerful and deeply resonant ways," said producers Wessex Grove and Gavin Kalin Productions. "Led by the extraordinary Bryan Cranston and Marianne Jean-Baptiste and brought to life by Ivo Van Hove and an exceptional design team, this production offers a compelling examination of the American Dream and the cost of putting self-interest above collective responsibility. At a moment when Miller's questions of accountability, truth, and moral responsibility feel more urgent than ever, we look forward to sharing this timely and deeply moving production with New York audiences."

articles.title: 5 Mutant Clones That the MCU Could Introduce With Mister Sinister On the Way
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics The X-Men are coming to the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), and the first main villain is going to be Mister Sinister. The biggest thing to note about Mister Sinister is that he is a master at cloning, and almost all of his stories in comics are about cloning mutants and even himself. The fact is […]
articles.content:
Of course, Mister Sinister isn't the only person to create clones in the Marvel Universe. There have been clones from the future who have almost destroyed the present day, and there are clones who have become heroes as well, making these such a huge part of the Marvel mutant universe. Any of these would fit perfectly in the MCU.

Stryfe made a cameo in The New Mutants #86 (1989) by Louise Simonson and Rob Liefeld. He made his first full appearance in The New Mutants #87. In the X-Men comics, Scott Summers sent his son Nathan into the future to find a cure for the techno-organic virus that Apocalypse infected the baby with. Knowing Cable's importance, Mother Askani created a backup clone of the baby just in case Cable didn't survive. That clone was Stryfe .

Apocalypse kidnapped the clone and named him Stryfe, planning to use him as a host body, but changed his mind when he learned the child was a clone. Because Stryfe was discarded when Cable survived, he grew up with a hatred of the hero and spent years as a mutant terrorist. His telepathy and telekinesis are stronger than Cable's because he was never infected with the techno-organic virus, and genetic experiments gave him superhuman strength and durability. If Mister Sinister's plot focuses on Scott Summers and Jean Grey, like in the comics, Stryfe is a possibility.

Fantomex is a unique case because he didn't start out as a clone. Fantomex debuted in New X-Men #128 (2002) by Grant Morrison and Igor Kordey. Instead of being a clone, Fantomex started out as an escaped Weapon Plus experiment designed as a mutant-hunting super-sentinel, born to a techno-organic mother fertilized with nanomachines, and raised in an artificial environment called the World. However, the cloning came later in his existence.

He uses E.V.A., a saucer-shaped techno-organic external nervous system that flies, reshapes, and fires energy. He also uses misdirection illusions, enhanced reflexes, healing, and marksmanship. After the Skinless Man killed him, E.V.A. cloned him, and his three brains split into three separate people: Weapon XIII, Cluster, and Fantomex. Fantomex could be a great addition to the MCU as a Weapon X clone, which could help him fit into whatever Marvel has planned for Wolverine's corner of the X-Men's world.

Joseph first appeared in a cameo in X-Men #46 (1995) by Scott Lobdell and Andy Kubert. His full debut came in Uncanny X-Men #327 by Lobdell and Roger Cruz, where he showed up as a man with magnetic powers and no memory who looked just like Magneto. The truth is that the teleporter Astra created him as a younger clone of Magneto for revenge and sent Joseph to kill Magneto. That said, most people assumed he was Magneto for a long time before this origin was revealed.

Joseph has Magneto's magnetic abilities, with more raw power but less skill and finesse than the original. He joined the X-Men to fight Onslaught, and then he fought in the “Magneto War,” where he merged with Earth's magnetosphere to neutralize a magnetic storm, dying in the process. At the moment, there is no Magneto in the X-Men's MCU reboot, but bringing in Joseph as a clone could be a great misdirect.

The Stepford Cuckoos debuted in New X-Men #118 (2001) by Grant Morrison and Ethan Van Sciver. They were grown from more than a thousand ova taken from Emma Frost while she lay in a coma after the Sentinel attack that killed her Hellions students. The only survivors were then named Celeste, Esme, Irma, Phoebe, and Sophie. They also come from the Weapon Plus program and were designed by Sublime to be mutant killers.

The Stepford Cuckoos have a telepathic group mind that grows stronger the closer the sisters are, plus telekinesis and the ability to turn into invulnerable diamond bodies. They are, basically, five teenage versions of Emma Frost. Two of them died. Sophie died stopping Quentin Quire's riot after using the drug Kick, and Xorn later killed Esme during “Planet X.” However, they were brought back thanks to the Resurrection Protocol on Krakoa. With Samara Weaving cast as Emma Frost, bringing in the Stepford Cuckoos is a possibility.

The most famous clone in X-Men history is Madelyne Pryor . Mister Sinister had plans for Scott Summers and Jean Grey, and he wanted to manipulate them into having a baby that he believed would have the power to beat Apocalypse. After Jean Grey died in “The Dark Phoenix Saga,” Sinister sent a clone he had created and programmed to believe she was a human named Madelyne Pryor to meet Scott and fall in love with him. They married and had a baby named Nathan Summers, completing Sinister's plans.

Madelyne Pryor debuted in Uncanny X-Men #168 (1983) by Chris Claremont and Paul Smith. After the baby was born, and following Jean Grey's return from the dead, Sinister sent the Marauders to kill Madelyne and steal the baby. Eventually, Madelyne realized the truth about herself and then developed psychic powers and sorcery, becoming the Goblin Queen. With Sadie Sink already in the MCU as Jean Grey, Marvel could plan out a way for Sinister to bring in Madelyne and make her the most likely clone to disrupt the X-Men's lives.

Which clones do you want to see appear in the MCU when the X-Men arrive? Let us know your favorite mutant clone stories in the comments below.
