articles.title: New GTA 6 Update Released by Rockstar Games on PS5 and Xbox
articles.summary: Rockstar Games has released the second update for GTA 6 ahead of its launch on November 19 on PS5, Xbox Series S, and Xbox Series X. The new update comes three days after the first-ever GTA 6 update was released on November 13. And like the first update, we do not know what this update […]
articles.content:
The new GTA 6 update is specifically labeled as Update 01.002.001 in the PlayStation and Xbox back end, per PlayStation Game Size . And it's smaller than the first update, which was roughly 1 GB in size. This second update is only 600 MB in size. This is a small download by update standards, and it begs the question: if it's so small, why did Rockstar Games feel the need to push it live? For those who do not know, it costs money to push updates live, among other things, which is why developers often prefer to accumulate fixes and changes in favor of releasing larger updates than a constant stream of smaller ones. To this end, this update doesn't do much, but it clearly does something important.

Both of the updates have been small, which suggests that if Rockstar Games is tweaking and fixing things, it's not tweaking and fixing much, which indirectly confirms it is happy with the state of the game and that it is polished. What is more likely, though, is that these are security updates for Grand Theft Auto VI , which we know Rockstar Games has gone above and beyond with for the release to ensure it doesn't leak.

Grand Theft Auto VI is set to release on November 19, in just three days, via PS5, Xbox Series S, and Xbox Series X. When it does, it will cost a minimum of $80. That said, those who don't have $80 to spend on it right now may be able to score a free code for it .

articles.title: 5 Sci-Fi Movie Spin-Offs That Were Better Than Expected, Including One That Surpassed the Original
articles.summary: Who doesn't love a good spin-off? It's an opportunity to give people more of a story they already love, especially when it comes to sci-fi. On the other hand, not every franchise needs one since the previous films have already explored everything that universe has to offer. Still, telling Hollywood that is actually pointless, isn't […]
articles.content:
So, with that in mind, here are 5 sci-fi spin-offs that are still real hits, highly recommended, and worth your time, as they give exactly what audiences want to see.

When Lightyear was released in 2022, many people wondered whether there was really a need for a movie about Buzz Lightyear without the other Toy Story characters, because everyone had already known him for decades. However, the idea here was to tell the story of the space adventure that supposedly inspired the creation of the action figure, which was pretty interesting — but also risky, as competing with the audience's love for such a popular franchise was never going to be easy, right? Well, the movie focuses entirely on Buzz as he and his crew get stranded on an unknown planet. So, determined to find a way back home, the space ranger starts conducting experiments with space travel, only to find out that these attempts come with some consequences, such as time dilation.

And it's great that, despite being a spin-off, the film doesn't stick to the Toy Story formula. Instead, it explores space travel, time jumps, aliens, and other situations that don't depend on the existence of the toys in any way. Sure, when you look at everything as a whole, some of its ideas aren't explored as well as they could have been . It also lacks the emotional impact Pixar usually brings to its movies, which is probably why it didn't work for everyone . Still, Lightyear is worth giving a try, both for fans who can be curious to see Buzz in a different setting and with a different vibe, and for sci-fi fans looking for a good animated feature.

After so many Transformers movies with more robots, explosions, and destruction, it was time for a change, because that alone wasn't going to keep people interested in the long run. That's where Bumblebee came in with an idea the franchise really needed: scaling down the story and focusing more on the characters. It's not like the previous films didn't have their fun moments, but watching another battle between the Autobots and Decepticons was starting to get repetitive. The spin-off is a prequel and follows the titular character in 1987, when the Autobot arrives on Earth, loses his memory, and ends up hiding in a junkyard. Then he meets Charlie (Hailee Steinfeld), a teenager who's also going through a difficult time and develops an unexpected friendship with him.

And here we don't see Bumblebee as just another fighting machine , because his relationship with Charlie is much more important, and it actually makes you care about both characters enough to stick around until the end. Yes, there are still action sequences, but everything feels more focused and has a purpose within the story. Another great decision was bringing back the robots' classic designs, something longtime fans were happy to see. In the end, Bumblebee brings together nostalgia, humor, and a simpler plot that gave the franchise a refresh, and it even earned some of the best reviews among the live-action Transformers movies . It doesn't reinvent the franchise, but it shows that sometimes all a series needs is a reminder of why people became fans of it.

Predator had already spawned six movies, including sequels and crossovers, but then Prey arrived as a prequel to show what fans wanted the entire time : a group of characters facing an extremely dangerous alien hunter and having to figure out who will survive. And that's the point of this spin-off, which actually surpassed the original for most people . The story takes place roughly 300 years before the first movie and follows Naru (Amber Midthunder), a young Comanche woman who wants to prove that she can be just as skilled a hunter as anyone else. But when a Predator shows up in her territory, she realizes she's dealing with a threat different from any other animal.

And there's no need for lengthy explanations about the creature's origins or references to the other movies, since the suspense at the heart of the story comes from the difference between the two sides of the confrontation. Besides, the fact that Naru doesn't have access to modern weapons or equipment makes things even better, as she has to rely on observing the enemy's behavior, understanding how it hunts, and figuring out how to use the environment to her advantage. She doesn't defeat it by being stronger, but by learning to think like someone who's being hunted, and that's the reason why Prey was well-received: it brings back all the tension and brutality of the original, but without trying to recreate it, and therefore, having its own identity in a different historical setting.

You know that feeling of franchise fatigue? Even though Star Wars still has a huge audience, the series has been dealing with it for a while now. But for a long time, it seemed like almost every story in this universe had to involve the Skywalker family in some way. So Rogue One: A Star Wars Story came in to change things up. Set shortly before the events of A New Hope , the movie follows Jyn Erso (Felicity Jones), a woman recruited by the Rebel Alliance for a dangerous mission: stealing the plans for the Death Star. Alongside Cassian Andor (Diego Luna) and the rest of the team, she must find a way to help the Rebels figure out how to defeat the Empire . But fans already know how this story ends, right?

The stolen plans are the very ones that allow Luke (Mark Hamill) to destroy the Death Star in the original movie. However, Rogue One makes this story more meaningful by showing who had to risk their lives to make that victory possible. So, forget about Jedi, heroes destined to save the galaxy, or characters with some connection to the Force; here, we're following ordinary people who chose to fight against a powerful regime, giving the movie a much more war-like feel, with a military vibe, espionage, sacrifices, and everything that comes with it. It's a different side of Star Wars than what audiences are used to , but one that connects perfectly with the main events of the saga. It showed there was still potential in this universe ; it just needs to be explored in the right way.

After seeing Wolverine so many times in the X-Men movies, the question was whether there was anything new left to explore in his story. Well, considering how much fans love the character, it was probably worth finding another journey. So Logan came along as an answer to that question, but in a pretty unusual way, since it left behind superhero genre conventions to deliver a personal story . It takes place in 2029, when mutants are nearly extinct, and Logan (Hugh Jackman) is living in hiding, older and with his healing abilities weakened. His daily routine mostly consists of taking care of a sick Charles Xavier (Patrick Stewart) until the two end up having to protect Laura (Dafne Keen), a young mutant with abilities similar to Wolverine's.

And there was no need to introduce another villain trying to take over the world or anything like that. After everything the protagonist had been through, it was much more interesting to explore the consequences of his violent past and see how he would deal with having someone to care for. And even though Logan has action scenes , the best part of the movie is the relationship between its characters; it doesn't need references or connections to X-Men for you to have a genuinely great experience. It's a mature production, considered a masterpiece by many fans, and one that manages to bring out all kinds of emotions. It's also a satisfying conclusion to Jackman's version of Wolverine (at least at the time).

articles.title: People Are Complaining About The Secret Lives Of Mormon Wives Spinoff (But I Get It, It's Weird)
articles.summary: Mormon Wives: Orange County doesn’t exactly live up to its name.
articles.content:
If you’ve ever watched The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives , you know there’s no shortage of drama. Just look at Taylor Frankie Paul, who’s had a swingers scandal, the cancellation of her season of The Bachelorette , custody issues with her children, and chaos surrounding production . But the Hulu reality series was popular and created a lot of buzz, so I was not surprised when they announced the spinoff, The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County , currently on the 2026 TV schedule . However, the fact that it feels like the majority of the women in the new show are not Mormon and that some aren’t even wives is a bit weird and an interesting choice, considering the title, and viewers (including myself) have taken notice.

It’s hard not to notice that The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County is a cast divided into two groups, with the women who are Mormons being outnumbered by the women who are not. In the season premiere, cast member Aspyn Ovard (who's got a memorable storyline about being part of a throuple) says, “We’ve all been shaped by Mormonism in one way or another,” which is a bit of a vague statement when we don’t know all the details of the backgrounds of many of these women, and even she makes it clear that she’s very closed off to the church and its teachings.

For a reality show that’s supposed to be centered around Mormons, The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County actually positions them to be the villains of the season. McCall DaPron, the older sister of the OG series’ Mayci Neeley, exhibits confrontational behavior. She gets into frequent clashes with other cast members, often leaving them to wonder whether it’s possible to keep this friend group together.

On Sunday, Brand's wife, Laura Brand, delivered some words on behalf of her husband on the Forgetting Sarah Marshall star's YouTube channel.

Brand said he was "not guilty for the offences I have been jailed for” and confirmed that he was incarcerated at Littlehey Prison, a jail for men who have been convicted of sexual offenses.

Debuting Polish director Sonja Orlewicz-Zakrzewska destigmatizes pole dancing in Tallinn Black Nights premiere " Exotic ."

"It still shocks so many people," she tells Variety .

"Most of the girls and boys from the pole dancing community have experienced some kind of ostracism. People associate it with men's erotic pleasure. It doesn't occur to them that you can do it just for yourself." Orlewicz-Zakrzewska is a pole dancer too. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Pole dancing blew my mind," she admits. "I wanted to show this environment as a sporting environment. In every big city, there are a dozen or so pole dancing studios. But when I was pitching this project, people would hear ‘pole dancing' and ask: ‘So it takes place in a nightclub?' There's nothing wrong with nightclubs or sex work, but these are very different things."

"Exotic" is produced by Magdalena Sztorc and Anna Zajączkowska (Mozaika Films) and sold by Pluto Film .

In the film, the characters – played by Jaśmina Polak, Magdalena Koleśnik and Monika Frajczyk – head to a sleepy, unassuming beach resort to train. Just like Orlewicz-Zakrzewska. "Exotic" was shot during one of the Exo Stars Camp editions she also attended in the past.

"There are all these international pole dancing stars. People come from all over the world, and it's all happening….There. I love absurdities and contrasts, so when I got out of the car and saw these two universes colliding, I knew I had to go back with a camera," she laughs.

With the help of its founder Martyna Dominikowska, Orlewicz-Zakrzewska ended up shooting with real-life participants and instructors. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"It was all scripted, but we threw our actors into a documentary setup. These classes and showcases were actually taking place," she recalls.

"One of the pole dancers, Gracjan, works as a mechanic on ships. He was supposed to be on his way to Gibraltar at the time of the shoot. He wanted to be a part of it so badly that he convinced his employer not only to find a replacement for the time she would be gone, but also to make sure he could disembark and fly to Poland. It's my favorite story from the film."

Orlewicz-Zakrzewska found pole dancing to be "very healing." However, her protagonist, Mila, struggles with self-worth. Her inner voice repeatedly tells her: "You don't belong here, girl."

"I don't want to speak for the rest of society, but I definitely have that internal voice. We are all each other's worst critics. I've been training for four years now, but when I started, I was convinced I wouldn't be able to identify with these dancers," she says.

"I've always questioned my choices and I guess that's reflected in the film. I've always asked myself: Why am I putting on makeup or dressing this way? I was afraid of my own femininity and I judged others. When I started my adventure with pole dancing and became someone unafraid of sky-high heels, I realized that my fear of being seen as ‘cheap' came directly from patriarchy."

Mila's partner, played by "Corpus Christi" star Bartosz Bielenia, isn't exactly supportive either.

"That character came from my conversations with girls in the pole dancing community. Their partners often pretend to be cool with it, but then their insecurities take over. They can see it liberates them, and that makes them feel threatened."

Orlewicz-Zakrzewska wanted to be authentic in showing the bodies in her film.

"Just because you're filming a woman's body doesn't mean it's male gaze. It's all about your intention," she notes.

"My cinematographer Adam Suzin is also a sportsman and has trained acrobatics, so we thought about it together. My dream is to witness the destigmatization of bodies in public spaces, especially in Poland, where we're still laced into a Catholic corset."

"I tried to show what it's like for me, a girl who is in this environment. You look at your body a lot, and the bodies of others. In the age of social media, we all have a very warped sense of how we think bodies should look. It was great to go to these sessions and see how different they are. Sometimes it's so awkward, and funny, seeing someone try to strike a pose but end up looking like a cockroach," she jokes. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"For me, a big lesson from pole dancing – which I tried to include in the film – is that attractiveness doesn't come from your perfectly sculpted buttocks. It comes from how you feel about yourself and your attitude."

"It's about being able to express yourself freely through your body."

articles.title: PS1 Classic From 1997 Now Available on PS5 for $2.39
articles.summary: A PS1 classic game from 1997 is now available on PS5 and PS4 for $2.39, 29 years later. The game in question is not just a PS1 game from 1997, but one of the best PS1 games from 1997, and it has never been cheaper on the PlayStation Store since its release there in June […]
articles.content:
In addition to one of the great PS2 trilogies for $0.10 more , PlayStation users can grab Cyan Productions and Red Orb Entertainment's 1997 adventure game, Riven, for a couple of dollars. For those unfamiliar with this game, it is the second game in the Myst series, which dates back to 1993, and the game of the same name. While not as influential as its predecessor, Riven was one of the great games of its year, and actually the best-selling game of 1997. At the time of its release, it was only available on PS1 and PC, but it also came to Sega Saturn the following year in 1998.

Then, in 2025, the PS1 version was re-released on the PS5 and PS4 PlayStation Store alongside its introduction to the library of PS Plus Premium, where it remains available for free for those subscribed to the most expensive tier of the Sony subscription service.

The Best-Selling Game of 1997 In 2026, adventure games like this are somewhat niche, but it wasn't always like this. In the 1990s, it was one of the biggest genres, as evidenced by Riven being the best-selling game of 1997.

Some of this success, if not much of it, was on the back of Myst , though, which was actually the best-selling PC game of all time for quite some time. Further, it is often cited as one of the best of its time and one of the most influential games of all time. Further, Riven is a direct sequel, meaning it's best to play Myst first. It picks up right after the events of Myst , and while it can be played and enjoyed without playing Myst , Riven is best played with this context.

It's worth noting that a remake was released in 2024 , and this remake actually earned an 86 on Metacritic, three points better than the original. To this end, those who didn't play the original may find it easier to visit it via the remake rather than the original for obvious reasons. Those who do have nostalgia for the original, though, will likely prefer it over the remake simply because nostalgia outweighs modern improvements. The original is also $22 cheaper on the PS Store right now.

articles.content:
Beyoncé has once again made Grammy history in becoming the first artist with 100 nominations, as “Morning Dew (Donk)” secures a nod for best R&B solo performance.

The pop singer dropped the long-unreleased “Morning Dew (Donk)” on July 4 ahead of the 20th anniversary of her sophomore album “B'Day.” The track was originally written by Beyoncé , Pharrell Williams, The-Dream and Darius Dixon, and produced by Beyoncé and Williams. “Morning Dew (Donk)” will compete in the best R&B solo performance category against Kehlani's “Out the Window,” Victoria Monét's “Let Me,” Jill Scott's “Pressha” and Tems' “What You Need.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Netflix’s 'Haunted Hotel' Renewed for Season 3 ‘Gordon,’ a Big Netflix Series From Argentina, Unpacked by Pablo Trapero and Star Rodrigo de la Serna

Beyoncé is no stranger to making Grammy history, breaking the record for most wins in 2023 with 32, after earning four awards from the Recording Academy that year. At the time, the award that put her over was best dance/electronic album for “Renaissance.” Before the 2023 Grammys , the record for most Grammy wins was held by the 31 claimed by classical music figure Georg Solti — a benchmark set all the way back in 1997 when he earned his final prize, for best opera recording. Solti died that same year.

With the 2026 TV schedule heading into the holiday season, many are likely preparing for their favorite yuletide programming and getting ready for other festivities. There's at least one reason a gathering away from a football stadium might be easier this year. Kansas City is set to host the New England Patriots on Dec. 21 and the San Francisco 49ers on Dec. 27, leaving Christmas Day free of a game-day obligation.

Kelce has already talked about looking forward to his first Christmas as a married man. Earlier this month, while promoting Tommy Hilfiger's winter collection, he told Women's Wear Daily he was excited to start new traditions with Swift. articles.title: Forget Doctor Strange, This is the Best Benedict Cumberbatch Role Ever & I Can Explain Why
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Thanks to the success of the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) and the fact that he appeared in three of the biggest MCU movies ever made, Benedict Cumberbatch remains best known to most fans as Doctor Stephen Strange. Strange has appeared in two of his own movies, starting with Scott Derrickson's Doctor Strange and its Sam […]
articles.content:
However, Benedict Cumberbatch has so much more in his career that eclipses what he did as Doctor Strange in the MCU. He has received two Oscar nominations, one for The Imitation Game and the second for The Power of the Dog . Still, Cumberbatch's best performance of his career came with his role as Sherlock Holmes in the BBC Sherlock series.

While Benedict Cumberbatch's role as Doctor Strange was seen by more people than anything else he has ever done, thanks to the Avengers movies and his Spider-Man appearance, his role as Sherlock Holmes is better all around , at least for his character. Sherlock debuted in 2010 from creators Mark Gatiss and Steven Moffat, and it stars Cumberbatch as the legendary detective, Sherlock Holmes, and Martin Freeman as Doctor John Watson. Both characters are based on the literary figures created by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle.

Airing on the BBC, the show was unique, especially for American audiences. There were four seasons, but each season had only three 90-minute episodes, each telling a different Sherlock Holmes mystery story. Through the four seasons (and one additional special), some of the most iconic Sherlock Holmes stories were adapted, including A Study in Scarlet (renamed “A Study in Pink”) in Season 1, The Hound of the Baskervilles (renamed “The Hounds of Baskerville”) in Season 2, “The Adventure of Charles Augustus Milverton” (renamed “His Last Vow”) in Season 3, and “The Adventure of the Final Problem” (renamed “The Final Problem”) in Season 4. The stand-alone special in 2016 was called “The Abominable Bride.”

There have been countless adaptations of Sherlock Holmes over the years, with names like Basil Rathbone, Peter Cushing, Jeremy Brett, and Robert Downey Jr. taking on the role, but Benedict Cumberbatch matches up to all of them. Not only that, but the BBC Sherlock series is one of the best adaptations on TV or in the movies based on its quality of storytelling and the look of the series. It doesn't get much better than this, and Cumberbatch is a big reason why.

What really sets this series apart is that it removes Sherlock Holmes from the era most of the previous adaptations used, and instead places him in present-day London. This allows the series to really delve into who Sherlock Holmes is as a character rather than just have him as the typical detective genius he is usually portrayed as. Moffat and Gatiss also do a great job framing the scenes, so the audience sees the clues as Sherlock sees them, and the editing shows how he finds them, making Cumberbatch's performance even more impressive. His dry wit, precision, and awe are inspiring, and his performance did more to make Sherlock Holmes a real person than anything before, including the Doyle stories.

There have been rumors of another Sherlock season since the fourth ended. There are plenty of stories that could still be told, but the fact that Cumberbatch has become such an in-demand actor and Freeman continues to get plenty of work makes the timing of actually doing another 270 minutes of stories hard to line up based on their schedules. While Moffat has said a fifth series was plotted by himself and Gatiss, it never happened.

Cumberbatch himself said he would like to do it, but Moffat said that Cumberbatch's movie career was not going to make it easy. Freeman even said never to close the door on another season, and he said he was interested in returning if the material was of good quality. However, things seem to have changed, as Gatiss said in 2025 that Cumberbatch and Freeman had decided they were no longer interested in returning for a new season, seeming to move on from the material and push forward with their careers. Interestingly enough, Robert Downey Jr. might have another Sherlock Holmes movie coming more than a decade after the last film was released, but it is Benedict Cumberbatch's version that really deserves another episode.

articles.content:
It's the end of an era at MS NOW ‘s Morning Joe .

Willie Geist, who has been a staple of the cable channel's morning show for nearly two decades, is exiting the program at the end of the year. The news was announced on Morning Joe Monday.

Geist, who also hosts Sunday Today on NBC, will instead take on an expanded role at NBC News and the Today show.

He was the last on-air personality to have a role at both NBC News and MS NOW, which split from NBC a year ago (he had been splitting time between MS NOW's Times Square studio and 30 Rockefeller Plaza). Other names, like Steve Kornacki, José Díaz-Balart and Jacob Soboroff, that worked for both brands ended up choosing one or the other. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Business Inside MS NOW's Post-Election Plans TV Savannah Guthrie Extends 'Today' Show Deal

Geist appeared almost daily as a co-host of Morning Joe alongside Joe Scarborough and Mika Brzezinski since 2007, while also leading Sunday Today , where he specialized in long-form interviews and features.

Geist began on MSNBC shortly after it canceled Don Imus, but before Morning Joe took over the timeslot full-time. He joined Today in 2012 as co-anchor of the 9 a.m. show, a role he held alongside his cable news job at Morning Joe and its spinoff Way Too Early , and moved to Sundays in 2016.

"I am so grateful to both NBC and MS NOW for the unique opportunity to do what I love at both networks," Geist said. "This is a bittersweet goodbye to Joe, Mika, and the place that made possible everything else in my career over the last two decades, but I am thrilled to settle in with my family at Today and dedicate all of my time to that special place.”

"Over the past 10 years, Willie has transformed Sunday Today from a broadcast into a distinctive, multi platform brand with a voice and identity all its own," said Libby Leist, executive VP of Today and lifestyle at NBC. "We're thrilled he'll now be able to focus full-time on building the brand in new ways and bringing his exceptional journalism to all of our platforms.”

articles.title: Willie Geist Will Exit MS NOW's 'Morning Joe' After Nearly 20 Years for Expanded Role at NBC's 'Today'
articles.summary: MS NOW mainstay “Morning Joe” transformed suddenly into "Morning Whoa!" Monday when Willie Geist, the program's longtime master of ceremonies, said he planned to leave his post at the end of the year for a broader role at NBC's “Today” franchise. The maneuver will break up an A.M. team — Geist, Joe Scarborough and Mika […]
articles.content:
MS NOW mainstay " Morning Joe " transformed suddenly into “Morning Whoa!” Monday when Willie Geist , the program's longtime master of ceremonies, said he planned to leave his post at the end of the year for a broader role at NBC's "Today" franchise.

The maneuver will break up an A.M. team — Geist, Joe Scarborough and Mika Brzezinski– that has stayed together for about two decades, a rarity in the world of early-bird TV. "Morning Joe" launched on the cable network once known as MSNBC in April of 2007. Scarborough and Brzezinski remain under contract with MS NOW through 2029. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Zarna Garg Sets Netflix Stand-Up Comedy Special (EXCLUSIVE) ‘Russell Brand: Open Secret’: Netflix Doc Reveals His ‘Jokes’ About Rape, Making a Girlfriend ‘Brush Her Teeth Until They Bled’ and More

"Joe and Mika are truly family to me," says Geist, during a recent interview with Variety . Being part of the program, which is a must-watch for a certain swath of inside-the-Beltway denizens as well as political aficionados, "has given me everything in my career," Geist adds. "I was a producer at MSNBC when Joe had the idea that I should be on set with him and Mika, which made not a lot of sense." Nonetheless, it worked: "Morning Joe" has become essential viewing, particularly for an influential audience niche, and is one of the Versant-backed outlet's signature programs.

After the start of 2027, Geist will get time to spend not only on the "Sunday Today" telecast he has led for more than a decade , but also on a variety of extensions that include a longform podcast of the show's main interview, known as a "Sunday Sitdown." He will contribute stories to "Today" that may have him travel around the country for human-interest pieces, or unique interviews. And he will fill in for various anchors when their schedules call them away from "Today's" weekday hours. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Geist has, for the past year, enjoyed one of the most unique arrangements in the TV-news business.

He works during the week for "Morning Joe," where he often keeps a roundtable conversation flowing from New York while Scarborough and Brzezinski typically weigh in from Florida, and then works to craft a Sunday telecast of NBC News ' "Today" that relies heavily on his writing sensibility and a deep-dive interview with a newsmaker or celebrity. He also fills in for various "Today" anchors like Craig Melvin and in the 10 a.m. hour as needed — a job that can pull him away from duties on "Morning Joe."

When MS NOW was part of the NBCUniversal media conglomerate, maintaining such a schedule — one in which he works in some capacity nearly every day of the week — was easier. Now that the cable-news outlet is part of a company, Versant, that was spun off from NBCU by corporate parent Comcast, the plan is more difficult to keep in motion.

"I think everyone agrees that this had to happen," Geist says.

Indeed, NBC News and MSNBC shared many personnel who contributed to both outlets, but only Geist was allowed to continue to do so following their split. Stephanie Ruhle and Steve Kornacki are among the journalists who had to pick sides , and NBC News in recent years has taken anchors who led hours on MSNBC, like Hallie Jackson and Craig Melvin, and gave them more duties at the broadcast operation.

"I was genuinely lucky to be able to do both," says Geist. "A lot of people didn't get that choice."

When MSNBC and NBC News were owned by the same company, studios for their programs were part of the company's complex at Rockefeller Plaza. Now that they've broken up, Geist finds himself hustling from Versant's headquarters through Times Square after "Morning Joe" ends to get over to NBC and tend to duties tied to "Today." There are times when he needs to be at "Today" during "Morning Joe," which can require him to leave one program early and rush over to join the other.

Geist's presence at "Morning Joe" has long been understated, but it is critical. He's the one who keeps the various contributors in New York teed up for commentary and reaction while Scarborough and Brzezinski offer viewpoints and perspective. Geist must be ready to spark conversation about a wide range of topics — and have some level of expertise in them all. "Part of the job I've loved at ‘Morning Joe' is it's a freewheeling conversation," says Geist. "You have to be ready for everything. We are going to talk about the political stores of the day in great detail, not just gloss over them, but also the discussion might turn to music or movies or sports, or whatever it is. It's a real morning breakfast conversation." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

In past interviews, Brzezinski and Scarborough have called their show partner essential. "The chemistry is Willie, Mika and me," Scarborough told Variety in 2020 , and when Geist takes off from the show on Mondays following his "Sunday Today" work, he said, "we really feel it."

"We hate it," Brzezinski added.

MS NOW did not immediately name a successor for Geist.

The show has fared well in recent months. "Morning Joe" is the most-watched cable-news morning program among viewers in Washington, D.C., and has, year to date, seen its overall audience hike 24%, according to data from Nielsen, while viewership among people between 25 and 54, the demographic most coveted by advertisers in news programs, increase 57%. The audience for Fox News Channel's “Fox & Friends,” however, is larger, as are the audiences for the three broadcast-network morning programs.

NBC News has spent more time working to monetize Geist's work on "Sunday Today." Once a quarter, he hosts one of his longform interviews in front of a paying audience in different parts of the country. NBC News in recent months has made a full video version of his "Sunday Sitdown” available on its digital platforms — a new way to reach audiences (and the advertisers who might follow them).

On TV, Geist says, the interview segments take up eight minutes, an eternity for the medium. Online, however, viewers may get 45 minutes to an hour of Geist quizzing subjects who over the years have included Mick Jagger, Paul McCartney or actor Ryan Reynolds.

"I like that, because nothing is lost," says Geist, who got his start in the business working for a CNN news venture with Sports Illustrated that hoped to vie with ESPN. "Everything we do is available to viewers and subscribers."

Geist will turn his focus to a Sunday program that has made some strides against its main competitor, CBS' "Sunday Morning." That program, a mainstay of the TV schedule, has seen its viewership decline this season, while the audience for Geist's show is on the rise.

Overall viewership for "Sunday Today" has risen 4% season to date as of November 8, according to data from Nielsen. Meanwhile, viewers between 25 and 54, the demographic coveted most by advertisers in news programming, are up 1%. The overall "Sunday Morning" audience is down 11% over the same period this season, while its demo viewership has fallen 9%. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Sunday Morning" continues to draw a bigger crowd than "Sunday Today." An average of 4.41 million viewers watched the CBS program as of November 8, compared with 2.72 million for "Sunday Today."

Sundays for Geist may be something of a family line of business. His father, the legendary writer and columnist Bill Geist, was an integral part of "CBS Sunday Morning" for 31 years.

When the younger Geist first started anchoring NBC's Sunday morning program, his father was still working at CBS' stalwart during the time slot. "There were mornings when you could look up" at TV monitors tracking news programs "and I would be on one and my dad would be on the other," Geist recalls. He grew up being a part of a Sunday-morning news audience, which would pay attention "on a day when people were able to stop and take the time and look and listen and were not racing" to get to work or school. "I love that show and was inspired by it," he says.

Was he destined to pick up similar duties? "I don't know if it was fated, or if it just happened that way," Geist offers. No matter what brought him to the time period, Geist's presence there appears to be locked in for the foreseeable future.

French film star Gérard Depardieu ( Green Card , Cyrano de Bergerac ) on Monday formally dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on the set of Jean Becker's The Green Shutters in 2021.

In a public statement sent to the French media, the actor accepted the 18-month suspended sentence, handed down by the French court last year , and admitted his guilt.

“The justice system has spoken. I have been found guilty. I hear it. I accept this and take full responsibility for the conviction,” Depardieu said in the statement, titled “I hear” released on Monday, shortly before his appeal trial was set to begin. “For a long time on film sets, I hid behind provocation and crude, suggestive humor,” the statement continued. "I believed my comments and actions to be without consequence. They were not, given they were coming from a powerful person such as myself at the time… I now understand that there is a boundary between impertinence and offense. Speaking to local media in the wake of the statement, Depardieu's defense lawyer Delphine Meillet said the decision had been fruit of "a long period of reflection and personal growth."

A French court last year found Depardieu found guilty of sexually grouping two women, a production designer and an assistant director, on the set The Green Shutters . The guilty verdict also mandated that Depardieu register on France's national sex offender registry.

The ruling was the first successful case made against Depardieu, who faces at least 20 separate public accusations of sexually inappropriate behavior, going back decades.
